messages:
emma-support: Hey team, customer (cust-ops) reporting a 5-10m window of 503/500s hitting hosted inference. They saw a bunch of "upstream inference worker killed" and SIGSEGV logs. Can we triage?

mike: Linking logs they pasted — looks like a popup of kernel errors around `prefetch_pipeline` + a quant swap 30s before spike.

cust-ops: FYI we saw ~15% error rate for ~8 minutes starting 12:14 UTC, clients got `503 Service Unavailable` and timeouts. No config changes on our end.

emma-support: Paste of error from runner: ```
[runner] 12:14:22 ERROR: upstream inference worker exited: signal 11 (segfault)
[runner] 12:14:22 ERROR: GPU0: device-side assert / kernel abort in prefetch_kernel.cu: line 412
[runner] 12:14:22 WARN: trying restart container, exit code 137
```

alice: That code path `prefetch_kernel` is touched during KV prefetch + quant swap. We rolled the quantized model swap in staging last week. @mike any recent deployment to hosted pool?

mike: @alice I see a deploy event at 12:13:48 from `deploy-bot` for `runtime:prefetch-optimizations` — small kernel change + quant path toggle.

deploy-bot: deploy 4680009999 -> runtime-prefetch-optimizations completed to hosted-pool-3 at 2026-02-10T12:13:48Z :shipit:

oncall-bot: @emma-support Escalation acknowledged. Paging eng-runtime oncall. Runbook: add fallback routing and pin model to previous variant while we investigate.

jay: I'll pick this up. First pass: reproduce locally on a small GPU with quant-swap toggle + high concurrent prefetch. Can someone capture the container core dump / nvcrash logs from the affected host?

emma-support: I have attached the host logs from hosted-pool-3: `host-3a-09` — nvcrash present, coredump uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/4680012345/core-host-3a-09.tar.gz (link: <redacted>).

mike: Quick mitigation applied: routing bypass to fallback cpu-quant model for customers in affected shard, increased restart backoff to reduce churn. Noted slight latency increase for those requests.

alice: Repro notes so far: increasing prefetch batch count + enabling quant swap at runtime triggers the same kernel abort on Ampere 80GB in ~90s with large context (2k tokens). Lowering prefetch concurrency prevents crash.

jay: Action items: (1) rollback `runtime-prefetch-optimizations` from hosted-pool-3, (2) capture full CUDA logs + run nvprof on repro, (3) add unit test that cycles quant swap with KV prefetch.

emma-support: Rolling back now on hosted-pool-3, will monitor. Notifying customer and offering credits.

cust-ops: Thanks, appreciate the quick response. Keep us posted on RCA and timeline for fix.

alice: RCA hypothesis: a race in kernel where prefetch writes into a buffer assumed contiguous after quant swap -> memory index out-of-range on some NV kernels -> device-side assert -> segfault. Will PR a guarded path to abort quant swap if prefetch active as short-term fix.

mike: I'll coordinate a canary deploy of the guarded swap path after we have a green repro test. For immediate postmortem we should include: host/kernel versions, quantization toggles, context length distribution, and the exact prefetch config used by the customer.

oncall-bot: Incident triage complete. Severity: high. Incident owner: jay. Next update ETA 30m.
